stories.headline: Claude Code's "don't ask again" button has been writing passwords into files that end up on GitHub
stories.summary: Approve a command with "Yes, and don't ask again" and Claude Code saves the full command, credentials included, in .claude/settings.local.json. GitGuardian found 31,088 secrets across 23,276 public repositories, 5,343 still valid. Docker images leak it too. Rotate exposed keys, then add the file to .gitignore and .dockerignore.
stories.take: Secret scanners tuned to key formats now miss credentials hidden inside the shell commands agents record.

stories.headline: Stripe lets AI agents move money, with approval rules set by the business
stories.summary: Stripe Treasury, already used by 24,000 businesses for read-only agent work, now gives agents write access: transfers, currency conversion and vendor payments. Refunds, payouts and outbound transfers need human approval by default; agent API keys can wave through small ACH transfers, say under $50. When an agent pays, who in your organisation owns the approval threshold?
stories.take: Payment controls now have to cover software holding its own API key, where they once assumed a human login.

stories.headline: Amazon: pen-testing AI agents on Cairn found and exploited an unknown flaw from one instruction

stories.headline: Claude Code's "don't ask again" button has leaked thousands of working passwords onto public GitHub
stories.summary: GitGuardian found 31,088 secrets in Claude Code's settings.local.json files on public GitHub, and 5,343 worked when detected. stories.headline: NVIDIA's Dynamo cuts wasted GPU time in reinforcement learning by routing, caching and recovering rollouts
stories.summary: NVIDIA Dynamo now serves as the inference layer for reinforcement learning rollouts. It routes repeated prompts to workers holding cached context, sends only weight changes between updates, and reroutes around failed workers. H Company reports up to 20% shorter training steps. Integrations exist for verl, NeMo RL, Slime and prime-rl.
stories.take: Rollout serving no longer has to be hand-built inside each training framework; a shared inference layer now handles it.

Separately, an Audited ZDR (zero data retention) tier routes only to providers with published independent audits. Baseten, Modal and Wafer are launch partners, with reports due by 8 December 2026. Switch the team-wide toggle on for regulated workloads once reports land.
stories.take: Zero-data-retention promises now get tested by independent auditors and tripwire prompts, where contracts once asked buyers for faith.

stories.headline: Thinking Machines' small open model loops its layers to act bigger on a laptop
stories.summary: Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling 2 Mini is a mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. Twelve middle layers repeat three times, so 24 stored layers behave like 48. Hugging Face's own tests put it at least comparable in informal vibe tests, which Hugging Face says need more validation, to Qwen3.8-27B. Pull it through llama.cpp or MLX and rerun your own coding tasks against your current local model.
stories.take: Hugging Face's informal tests put a compressed local multimodal model on par with Qwen3.8-27B for coding.

sections.synthesis: Most of these gains come from the vendors' own figures: Dynamo's 20% from H Company, Inkling 2 Mini's 79.2% from its makers. The two voice and gateway items are cheap to try, so start there, and rerun the model claims on your own workloads.

Z.ai plans to open the weights after safety hardening; for now, access needs its Coding Plan subscription.

stories.headline: Researcher's 2 million planted secrets show prompts leak through AI routers like OpenRouter
stories.summary: If this holds, the AI supply chain is leakier than vendors imply. HD Moore seeded 2 million unique fake credentials and URLs into prompts, each sent to one provider. OpenRouter has since emailed customers that some prompts may have been read via MiniMax and three resellers, and removed its Zero Data Retention label from MiniMax endpoints.

stories.headline: Google open-sources a test of whether AI assistants can read a user's one-sided story
stories.summary: If this holds, assistant testing moves beyond absurd-claim traps. Google Research built simulations where a hidden-motive character acts, the user's agent consults the assistant, and the true motive is known by construction. stories.headline: Google DeepMind's agent teams cut quantum fusion simulation costs 11.8-fold, with every result proof-checked
stories.summary: If this holds, proof-checking could make AI-found quantum circuits trustworthy before hardware exists. Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 agent teams cut one fusion calculation's cost 11.8x, and each result was proved in the Lean theorem prover. The Lean library, problem specifications and verified solutions are public on GitHub; still too costly for early quantum computers.
stories.take: Quantum algorithm gains now arrive with machine-checked proofs, where they once rested on hand derivation by specialists.

stories.headline: Axiom's AI agents machine-check the longest proof in mathematics, all 15,000 pages of it

Axiom Math says its AI swarm formally verified the classification of finite simple groups, split into about 100 milestones and 43 million lines of code, then the 7,500-page Stacks project. stories.take: Checking a proof of this size no longer depends on specialists reading five hundred journal articles by hand.

stories.headline: Ai2 interviewed 17 scientists on where AI agents need guardrails before they run research
stories.summary: Ai2 interviewed 17 scientists across natural, applied and social sciences and found five dimensions of trust: validation, privacy, objectivity, accountability and transparency. Its proposals include benchmarks that test whether a literature-review agent misses contradictory evidence, or a coding agent opens files outside its authorised scope. These remain proposals to test with scientists.
stories.take: Agent benchmarks for science now get proposed to score research conduct, where they once scored only answer accuracy.

sections.synthesis: Most of these items put a checkable answer behind a claim that used to rest on trust: proofs in Lean, planted credentials, motives known by construction. They sit in Currents because each is one team's result so far, not yet repeated elsewhere.

digest.lead: A convenience button leaked live passwords.
digest.sentence: GitGuardian found 5,343 working secrets among 31,088 saved in Claude Code's local settings files across public repositories.
Told only to obtain shell access, agents on the Cairn framework found an unknown flaw and took over a university server.

digest.lead: A capable coding model fits locally.
digest.sentence: Ollama now runs Inkling 2 Mini, scoring 79.2% on SWE-Bench Verified, on Apple silicon Macs with 20GB.
Axiom Math says its agents formally verified the classification of finite simple groups, and caught several mistakes in the human original.
